Overview

The complete data-science lifecycle — from Python to production GenAI.

A 24-week, 120-session program that takes you from Python and statistics through machine learning, deep learning and computer vision, NLP and Generative AI, to SQL and Power BI — finishing with an end-to-end analytics system.

Starts from programming fundamentals and environment setup.

Built for

  • Aspiring data scientists who want the complete lifecycle
  • Analysts ready to move into machine learning
  • Engineers and developers transitioning into AI
  • STEM graduates building a data-science portfolio

24 weeks · 120 sessions

One lifecycle. Six transformations.

Watch the same data move through every stage of the craft — from a raw table to statistics, models, neural networks, language and finally the dashboard that drives the decision.

Full curriculum

Month 01 · Weeks 1–4 · Days 1–20

Python Programming, Data Handling & EDA Foundation

Week 1 Core Programming and Data Structures

Day 1Introduction to Programming & Environment Setup

A foundational start, defining programming as the process of creating a sequence of instructions to automate tasks. We'll explore Computational Thinking, breaking complex problems into manageable steps, and the critical distinction between an Algorithm (the step-by-step procedure) and a Program (the implementation of the algorithm in code). Environment setup is crucial: Installation of Anaconda (a distribution for Python and R that simplifies package management), selection of an Integrated Development Environment (IDE) like VS Code or a cloud-based solution like Google Colab, and executing basic interactive commands within a Jupyter Notebook environment.

Day 2Variables & Data Types

Dive into the mechanics of Python. Understanding the importance of correct Python Syntax and the rules for creating Identifiers (names for variables, functions, etc.). Introduction to the essential print() function for output. Focus on Python's dynamic typing with core Data Types: int (integers), float (floating-point numbers), string (text), and boolean (True/False). Learn to inspect data types using the type() function, capture user input with input(), and master type casting (explicitly converting one data type to another).

Day 3String Manipulation & Formatting

Text data is ubiquitous. This day covers advanced handling of the string data type. Techniques include String Indexing (accessing individual characters), Slicing (extracting substrings), and essential String Operations/Methods such like .upper(), .lower(), .replace(), and .split(). Crucially, we master modern string formatting using f-strings (formatted string literals) for readable and efficient code output.

Day 4Data Structures & Mutability

A deep dive into Python's powerful built-in Data Structures. We explore Lists (ordered, mutable, allows duplicates), Sets (unordered, mutable, unique elements), Tuples (ordered, immutable, allows duplicates), and Dictionaries (unordered, mutable, key-value pairs). A key conceptual focus is understanding Mutability vs Immutability, which dictates how an object can be changed after creation and affects performance and safety.

Day 5Operators in Python

Mastering the tools for computation and logic. Comprehensive coverage of Arithmetic Operators (+, -, *, /, //, %, **), Comparison Operators (==, !=, >, <, >=, <=), and Logical Operators (and, or, not). Practical application of Assignment Operators (=, +=, -=, etc.) and Membership Operators (in, not in) for checking existence within sequences.

Week 2 Control Flow, Functions, and I/O

Day 6Control Flow & Conditional Statements

Learning to control the execution path of a program. Implementation of the core decision structures: if, elif (else if), and else statements. Exploration of nested conditions for complex logic and applying conditional logic to build practical, real-world decision-making structures. Introduction to the range() function as preparation for loops.

Day 7Loops & Iterations

Automating repetitive tasks. Utilizing while loops (for indefinite iteration) and for loops (for definite iteration, typically over a sequence). Understanding nested loops for multi-dimensional operations (like matrices). Control loop behavior with pass (placeholder), break (exit loop), and continue (skip current iteration). Conclude with an introduction to efficient, concise code writing using List and Dictionary comprehensions.

Day 8Functions Basics

The cornerstone of modular programming. Focus on defining functions (def), understanding the different types of functions (built-in, user-defined), and the critical concepts of parameters (inputs) and return values (outputs). Introduces the concept of code optimization and conciseness using single-expression Lambda functions (anonymous functions).

Day 9Advanced Functions & Modules

Extending functional programming. Deep dive into Higher-order functions: map (apply a function to all items), filter (filter items based on a function), and reduce (cumulative computation). Learn to import and utilize external modules and packages, understanding namespace and scope. Utility functions like help() and dir() are introduced. Practical work with built-in modules: math, random, datetime, and os (Operating System).

Day 10File Handling & Exceptions

Making programs robust and capable of data persistence. Detailed session on handling errors and exceptions using try, except, else, and finally blocks to gracefully prevent program crashes. Practical file input/output operations: creating, reading, and writing files in various common formats such as plain TXT, structured CSV, and semi-structured JSON.

Week 3 Object-Oriented Programming (OOP), Regex, and Web Scraping

Day 11Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) Fundamentals

Shifting to an object-centric paradigm. Understanding the OOP Philosophy and its advantages. Learning to create Classes (blueprints) and instantiate Objects (instances). Key components are Attributes (data/state) – specifically Instance and Class Variables – and the mandatory __init__ constructor method for object initialization.

Day 12Advanced OOP Concepts

Deeper exploration of class functionality. Implementing Instance Methods, Class Methods (@classmethod decorator for methods bound to the class), and Static Methods (@staticmethod for utility functions within a class). Comprehensive coverage of the Four Pillars of OOP: Encapsulation (data hiding using access modifiers), Inheritance (creating new classes from existing ones), Abstraction (showing only essential information), and Polymorphism (one interface, many forms).

Day 13OOP Implementation & Magic Methods

Practical application of OOP. Techniques include Method Overriding (redefining a parent's method in a child class) and using the super() function to call parent methods. Introduction to Special/Magic Methods (e.g., __str__, __len__). Concluding with the use of Abstract Base Classes (ABC module) for enforcing structure and a hands-on project: building a simple Console-Based Student Management System using all OOP concepts learned.

Day 14Unstructured Data & Regular Expressions

Handling real-world data complexity. Differentiating between Structured, Semi-Structured, and Unstructured Data. Mastering Regular Expressions (Regex), including Regex Literals and Meta Characters (., *, +, ?, [], etc.) for pattern matching. Practical focus on cleaning text data (e.g., removing noise) and validation tasks, such as Email validation.

Day 15Web Scraping Basics

The first step in data acquisition from the web. Learn the concept of Data Collection (web-scraping): programmatically extracting data from websites. The goal is converting the initial unstructured web data (HTML) into structured formats (like a Pandas DataFrame) suitable for analysis and generating insights.

Week 4 NumPy, Pandas, and EDA Capstone

Day 16NumPy (Numerical Python)

The backbone of numerical computing in Python. Introduction to the ndarray (N-dimensional array). Mastering Array creation, basic printing, indexing, slicing, and reshaping arrays. Key topics include fundamental Basic operations, mathematical functions (trigonometric, exponential), and the efficiency of Broadcasting and Vectorization when compared to traditional Python loops.

Day 17Pandas Fundamentals

The essential library for data manipulation and analysis. Introduction to the two core data structures: Series (1-dimensional) and DataFrames (2-dimensional, tabular). Practical application in Data importing and exporting using common formats like CSV, Excel, JSON files, and even data extracted from HTML tables. Initial steps involve using basic data understanding operations like .head(), .info(), and .describe().

Day 18Advanced Pandas & Data Manipulation

Deepening Pandas proficiency. Techniques for data selection: Indexing (.loc, .iloc), Slicing, and Conditional Filtering. Essential data summarization with GroupBy operations. Comprehensive coverage of Handling Missing Data (categorizing as MCAR, MAR, MNAR, and implementing Imputation techniques). Other cleaning tasks include Removing Duplicates and practical String/DateTime Manipulations.

Day 19Data Merging & Feature Engineering

Integrating and preparing data for modeling. Techniques for combining DataFrames: Concatenating (stacking), Merging (SQL-style joins), and Joining (index-based joins). Introduction to Window Functions (e.g., rolling means). Essential Feature Engineering concepts: Outlier detection using statistical methods (IQR, Z-score) and a critical discussion on addressing data leakage to ensure model integrity.

Day 20Month 1 Capstone & Consolidation

A culmination of Month 1 skills. This day focuses on integrated, Comprehensive Case Studies that require synthesizing knowledge of Python, functions, and data manipulation with Pandas. A key component is applying Web Scraping from scratch to acquire data, followed by thorough data cleaning and preparation using the advanced Pandas techniques learned.

Month 02 · Weeks 5–8 · Days 21–40

Statistics, Exploratory Data Analysis & Probability

Week 5 Visualization and Descriptive Statistics

Day 21Data Visualization with Matplotlib

The foundational plotting library. Understanding the Principles of basic plotting (figure and axes). Mastering the creation of subplots for multi-panel visualizations and customizing properties (titles, labels, colors). Hands-on building of fundamental plot types: Line plots, Pie Charts, Bar Graphs, Histograms (for distribution), and Scatterplots (for correlation).

Day 22Data Visualization with Seaborn

A high-level, statistically-focused visualization library built on Matplotlib. Constructing complex statistical plots like Box and Violin Plots (for distributions and comparisons), Joint Plots (bivariate analysis), Cat Plots (categorical data), Heatmaps (for correlation matrices), Pair Plots (all pairwise relationships), and Count plots (frequency).

Day 23Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)

The art of uncovering insights before modeling. Understanding the goals of EDA (data cleaning, structure identification, outlier detection, hypothesis generation). Practical steps in Uni-Variate (single variable) and Bi-Variate (two variables) Analysis. Focusing on Distribution analysis, creating a Correlation matrix to quantify relationships, and Trend identification in time-series or sequential data.

Day 24Descriptive Statistics

Quantifying data characteristics. Defining the distinction between Population vs Sample and Parameter vs Statistic. Reviewing Data Types (Nominal, Ordinal, Interval, Ratio). In-depth study of Measures of Central Tendency: Mean (average), Median (middle value), and Mode (most frequent value), and when to use each.

Day 25Measures of Dispersion & Shape

Assessing data spread and form. Methods for quantifying variability: Calculating Variance, Standard deviation (the square root of variance), Range, and the Interquartile Range (IQR). Understanding data shape using Skewness (asymmetry) and Kurtosis (peakedness). Utilizing Box Plots as a visual tool for measuring dispersion and effective outlier detection.

Week 6 Probability and Distributions

Day 26Probability Basics

The foundation of statistical inference. Defining Experiments, Sample Space, Events, and the calculation of classical probability. Covering the fundamental Probability rules/axioms (e.g., addition rule, multiplication rule).

Day 27Conditional Probability

Probability based on prior information. Understanding the relationship between Independent vs dependent events. In-depth study and application of Bayes Theorem (reversing conditional probability) for practical scenarios like spam detection.

Day 28Probability Distributions & Random Variables

Modeling uncertainty. Defining Random Variables (variables whose values are outcomes of random events). Distinguishing between Discrete (countable outcomes) and Continuous (any value in a range) probability distributions, and the difference between PMF (Probability Mass Function) and PDF (Probability Density Function).

Day 29Advanced Distributions

Key distributions used in data science. Detailed analysis of Bernoulli (single trial), Binomial (multiple Bernoulli trials), and Poisson (count of events over time/space) distributions for discrete data. Mastering the Normal Distribution (bell curve), Standard Normal Distribution (Z-scores), Z-distribution, and T-distribution for continuous data and inference.

Day 30Data Gathering & Sampling Methods

Techniques for collecting representative data. Reviewing different methods to select a subset of the population: Convenience, Simple Random, Stratified (proportional representation), Cluster (group-based), and Systematic Sampling.

Week 7 Inferential Statistics and ML Introduction

Day 31Inferential Statistics

Drawing conclusions about a population from a sample. Understanding Sampling variability and the cornerstone theorem: the Central Limit Theorem (CLT). Practical application in defining and calculating Confidence Intervals (CI) to estimate population parameters.

Day 32Hypothesis Testing Fundamentals

Formalizing statistical decision-making. The process of Setting Null (H0) & alternative (Ha) hypotheses. Understanding the critical concepts of p-value, significance level (α), and the risks involved: Type I Error (α, false positive) and Type II Error (β, false negative).

Day 33Parametric vs Non-Parametric Tests

Selecting the appropriate statistical test. Distinguishing between tests that assume a distribution (parametric) and those that do not (non-parametric). Executing tests for normality (e.g., Shapiro-Wilk), and implementing the workhorse tests: Z-tests (large sample, known σ) and T-tests (small sample, unknown σ).

Day 34Advanced Hypothesis Testing

More complex comparative and association tests. Practical application of A/B testing (comparing two groups), Chi-Square Tests (for categorical association), F-Tests (comparing variances), and ANOVA (Analysis of Variance for comparing means of 3 or more groups).

Day 35Introduction to Machine Learning Workflow

The transition to predictive modeling. Defining Supervised vs Unsupervised Learning. Overview of various algorithms' approaches (e.g., geometric, probabilistic). Critical discussion of the Bias-variance tradeoff as the central challenge in model building (underfitting vs. overfitting).

Week 8 Pre-processing and Simple Regression

Day 36Data Pre-processing for ML

Preparing data for optimal model performance. Techniques for pre-processing Tabular, text, and image data. Key focus on identifying and diagnosing model fit: under fit (high bias), optimal fit, and over fit (high variance) scenarios. Practical implementation of building robust data processing pipelines using sklearn.

Day 37Model Validation Methods

Ensuring generalizability of the model. Implementing and understanding various methods to estimate a model's performance on unseen data: Hold-out validation, Cross-Validation, the exhaustive Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation (LOOCV), and the industry-standard k-Fold Cross-Validation.

Day 38Simple Linear Regression

The foundation of predictive modeling. Understanding the Simple Linear Regression equation (ŷ = β0 + β1x1). Techniques for estimating coefficients using the method of Ordinary Least Squares (OLS). Crucial review of the OLS Assumptions (linearity, homoscedasticity, independence, normality of errors).

Day 39Multiple & Polynomial Regression

Extending the linear model. Expanding to Multiple Regression (ŷ = β0 + β1x1 + … + βnxn). Techniques for estimating regression coefficients in multivariate settings. Identifying and mitigating Multicollinearity. Handling non-linear relationships with Polynomial Regression, including detecting feature interactions, and methods for feature selection (forward, backward, stepwise).

Day 40Optimization & Regularization

Improving model training and preventing overfitting. Introduction to the fundamental optimization algorithm: Gradient Descent (including Batch, Stochastic, and Mini-Batch variants). Defining Cost functions (or Loss functions). Implementing Regularization techniques to penalize complex models: L1 (Lasso) (for feature selection), L2 (Ridge) (for shrinking coefficients), and ElasticNet (a combination of both).

Month 03 · Weeks 9–12 · Days 41–60

Supervised & Unsupervised Machine Learning

Week 9 Regression and Classification Metrics

Day 41Evaluation Metrics for Regression

Quantifying regression model performance. Deep dive into Residual Analysis (plotting errors). Using the Q-Q Plot to check for normality of residuals. Identifying the line of best fit. Essential metrics: Mean Squared Error (MSE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), R Squared (coefficient of determination), and the penalty-adjusted Adjusted R Squared.

Day 42Logistic Regression

Classification using a linear approach. Understanding the Difference between Regression and Classification (predicting a value vs a class). The mathematical basis: the Logit/Sigmoid functions to squash output between 0 and 1. Defining decision boundaries and the crucial process of setting thresholds to convert probabilities into discrete classes.

Day 43Classification Evaluation Metrics

Comprehensive assessment of classification models. Mastering the Confusion Matrix (True Positives, False Negatives, etc.). Calculating key metrics: Accuracy, Error rate, Precision (purity), Recall (completeness), and the harmonic mean F1 Score. Understanding TPR/FPR (True/False Positive Rates) and the ROC-AUC (Receiver Operating Characteristic - Area Under the Curve) for threshold-independent performance.

Day 44Naive Bayes Classifier

A fast and simple probabilistic classifier. Understanding the Principles of Naive Bayes, which assumes feature independence. Defining Posterior (what we want to find), Prior (initial belief), and Likelihood (how well data fits hypothesis) probability. Exploring different practical types of Naive Bayes: Multinomial (for counts/text), Bernoulli (binary features), Gaussian (continuous data), and Categorical.

Day 45K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN)

A non-parametric, instance-based learning algorithm. Detailed exploration of the K-Nearest Neighbor Algorithm mechanics. Choosing appropriate distance metrics (Euclidean, Manhattan). The problem of the Curse of Dimensionality in KNN. Distinguishing between Eager vs Lazy learners. Practical application of Hyperparameter tuning (selecting the optimal 'K').

Week 10 SVM, Trees, and Ensemble Methods

Day 46Support Vector Machines (SVM) - Part 1

A powerful classifier based on hyperplanes. Understanding the core concept: the Maximal Margin Classifier. Defining HyperPlanes, Support Vector Classifiers, and the difference between Hard vs Soft Margin Classification (allowing some misclassification).

Day 47Support Vector Machines (SVM) - Part 2

Handling non-linear data with SVM. Techniques for Classification with Non-linear Decision Boundaries. The genius of the Kernel Trick for mapping data to higher dimensions, focusing on the Polynomial and Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernels. Practical knowledge on Tuning Hyper parameters like Gamma, Cost (C), and Epsilon (ε).

Day 48Decision Trees

An interpretable, rule-based model. Mastering Basic Terminology: Root Node, Internal Nodes, and Terminal Node (Leaf). Distinguishing between Classification vs Regression trees. The process of evaluating split quality using metrics like the Gini Index and Entropy (information gain).

Day 49Tree Optimization

Improving the performance and generalizability of trees. Methods for Handling Overfitting in complex trees through Pruning (reducing tree complexity) and setting Stopping Criteria (e.g., minimum leaf size). Accuracy Estimation using cross-validation. Implementing automated Hyper parameter tuning using efficient methods like random search and grid search.

Day 50Ensemble Methods & Random Forest

Combining multiple models for better performance. Core Concepts of Ensemble Learning (bagging, boosting). Understanding Bootstrap Aggregation (Bagging). Deep dive into Random Forest mechanics: utilizing random subsets of features and data. Determining Variable selection and feature importance. Analyzing the OOB (Out-of-Bag) error estimate.

Week 11 Boosting and Dimensionality Reduction

Day 51Boosting Algorithms

Sequentially building models to correct previous errors. Implementing classic and modern boosting techniques: Adaboost (Adaptive Boosting), Gradient Boosting, and the highly efficient XG Boosting (eXtreme Gradient Boosting). Comprehensive review of key Hyper parameters, Pros, and Cons of these powerful boosting methods.

Day 52Intro to Unsupervised Learning

Discovering patterns in unlabeled data. Understanding the core Challenges of Unsupervised Learning. The key difference in goal: Clustering (grouping data) vs Classification (predicting a label).

Day 53Dimensionality Reduction - PCA

Principal Component Analysis for feature space compression. Defining Principal Components (new orthogonal axes), EigenValues (variance along axes), and EigenVectors (direction of axes). The property of Orthogonality. The mathematical process of Transforming data and calculating the proportion of variance explained (scree plot analysis).

Day 54Dimensionality Reduction - t-SNE

A non-linear technique for visualization. Understanding the complex Mechanics of t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE) for visualizing high-dimensional data in 2D/3D space. Comparative case studies highlighting the strengths and weaknesses of PCA (linear) and t-SNE (non-linear, locally focused).

Day 55K-Means Clustering

A centroid-based partitioning algorithm. The iterative process of Establishing Centroids and Medoids. Crucially, methods for deciding the optimal 'k' (number of clusters) using the Elbow Method/Inertia and evaluating cluster quality with the Silhouette score.

Week 12 Advanced Clustering and Capstone

Day 56Hierarchical Clustering

Building a hierarchy of clusters. Distinguishing between Divisive (top-down) vs Agglomerative (bottom-up) Clustering. Interpreting the results using Dendrograms (tree-like diagrams). Understanding different Linkage Methods (single, complete, average) and exploring practical clustering applications.

Day 57DBSCAN

Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise. The core concepts of Density-based clustering. Identifying data points as core points, border points, and noise (outliers) based on neighborhood density.

Day 58Applied Machine Learning - Part 1

Real-world application of ML models. Focus on advanced techniques for Missing Value imputation using sophisticated Machine Learning Algorithms (e.g., using regression to predict missing values, or MICE).

Day 59Applied Machine Learning - Part 2

Another critical real-world application. Utilizing Machine Learning Algorithms (e.g., Isolation Forest, One-Class SVM) for Outlier and Anomalies detection in datasets, crucial for fraud detection or system monitoring.

Day 60Month 3 Capstone & ML Deployment Basics

The final project for supervised/unsupervised learning and the first taste of MLOps. Developing and serving a functional Machine Learning Application. Utilizing Streamlit (a Python library) for creating a simple web interface. The culmination is a Customer Segmentation (unsupervised) or a classification (supervised) mini-project.

Month 04 · Weeks 13–16 · Days 61–80

Deep Learning & Computer Vision

Week 13 Deep Learning Fundamentals and ANNs

Day 61Introduction to Deep Learning

Setting the context for neural networks. Clarifying the hierarchy: AI vs ML vs DL. A brief History of Deep Learning (from perceptrons to modern ANNs). Understanding the functional analogy between Biological Neurons vs Perceptrons (the fundamental building block).

Day 62Deep Learning Frameworks

Introducing the tools of the trade. Setting up and utilizing Google Colab for cloud-based GPU access. Introducing TensorFlow (Google's framework) with basic syntax for tensor operations. Understanding TensorFlow Graphs and using TensorBoard for model visualization and debugging.

Day 63Artificial Neural Networks (ANN)

The core structure of Deep Learning. Understanding the Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) Architecture (input, hidden, output layers). The process of Forward Propagation (data flowing through the network) and training a simple single neuron model (perceptron).

Day 64Backpropagation Mechanics

The engine of neural network learning. In-depth understanding of the chain rule in calculus as applied to network training. The process of memorization in Backpropagation (adjusting weights based on error) and the critical step of calculating weight updates for each layer using the computed gradients.

Day 65Activation Functions

Introducing non-linearity into the network. Addressing the critical issues of the vanishing and exploding gradient problems. Implementing and understanding the properties of classic and modern functions: Sigmoid, Tanh, ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit), and the ReLU Variants (Leaky, Parametric, ELU, SELU).

Week 14 Optimization, Keras, and Image Prep

Day 66Optimizers & Loss Functions

Driving the network towards convergence. Distinguishing between Convex vs Non-Convex Functions in the loss landscape. Identifying and navigating Saddle Points. Implementing and comparing various advanced Optimizers: SGD with Momentum, NAG, RMSprop, AdaDelta, AdaGrad, ADAM, and NADAM.

Day 67Regularization & Tuning in DL

Strategies for building robust, non-overfitting networks. Overcoming DNN failures by implementing Dropouts (randomly ignoring neurons), Batch Normalization (stabilizing learning), various Weight Initialization Techniques (e.g., Xavier, He), and Early Stopping (halting training when validation loss stalls).

Day 68Applied Keras & TensorFlow (Regression)

Hands-on model construction. Focus on the high-level API Keras for simplified network building. Hands-on model building: Constructing a Regression model (predicting a continuous value) using the MLP architecture with the Keras Sequential API.

Day 69Deep Learning for Classification

Applying ANNs to classification tasks. Hands-on model building: Constructing a Classification model (predicting a category) using the MLP architecture. Implementing appropriate activation functions (e.g., softmax) and loss functions (e.g., cross-entropy) in Keras.

Day 70Image Processing Foundations

The gateway to Computer Vision. Introduction to OpenCV (Open Source Computer Vision Library). Understanding how images are formed/stored (pixels, channels). Exploring different color spaces (RGB, Grayscale). Practical operations: reading/writing/saving images, and capturing live data via webcam.

Week 15 Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN)

Day 71Advanced OpenCV

Extending image manipulation. Techniques for Drawing on images/videos (shapes, text). Understanding bitwise operators for image masking. Building image histograms to analyze intensity distribution. Distinguishing between Affine vs Non-Affine Transformations for geometric adjustments.

Day 72Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) Intro

The architecture for image understanding. The fundamental question: Why CNN over MLP for images? Detailed breakdown of how convolution works (filters/kernels), the purpose of Padding (maintaining size), Stride (movement of the filter), and the function of Pooling layers (downsampling).

Day 73CNN Architectures - Part 1

Studying landmark network designs. Understanding and implementing the structure of early network structures: LeNet5 (pioneering CNN for digit recognition) and AlexNet (the winner of the 2012 ImageNet challenge, proving the power of deep CNNs).

Day 74CNN Architectures - Part 2

Deepening the understanding of state-of-the-art models. In-depth study of the architectures: VGG16 and VGG19 (focus on depth using 3x3 kernels), Inception Net (GoogLeNet) (using multi-size filters), and ResNet (Residual Networks) (solving the degradation problem with skip connections).

Day 75Advanced Architectures & Case Study

Exploring highly efficient and modern designs. Introduction to Xception (depthwise separable convolution), MobileNet (efficient for mobile/edge devices), and EfficientNet (scaled architecture). Concluding with an Image Classification Case Study: Face Mask Detection.

Week 16 Transfer Learning and Object Detection

Day 76Transfer Learning

Leveraging pre-trained knowledge. Defining What is Transfer Learning? Understanding When and why to use it (e.g., small datasets). Practical skill: Coding Transfer Learning pipelines (feature extraction and fine-tuning) for custom datasets (e.g., Bone fracture multi-region detection).

Day 77CNN Hyperparameter Tuning

Optimizing Deep Learning models. Utilizing automated search techniques for model optimization: Random Search, the highly efficient Hyperband, and the probabilistic Bayesian optimization.

Day 78Object Detection Fundamentals

Locating and classifying multiple objects in an image. Introduction to the classic Object Detection algorithms: R-CNN (Region-based CNN), Fast R-CNN, and the region proposal network-based Faster R-CNN.

Day 79YOLO (You Only Look Once)

The modern, real-time object detection standard. Understanding the YOLO algorithm mechanics (a single-shot detector). Practical Implementation of YOLO v7/v8 using Ultralytics for high-speed, accurate detection.

Day 80Month 4 Capstone

The final Computer Vision project. A complete, integrated project: Building a real-time Helmet Detection or Plant Disease Prediction system using the latest techniques like YOLO for detection/localization and Transfer Learning for backbone model utilization.

Month 05 · Weeks 17–20 · Days 81–100

Natural Language Processing (NLP) & Generative AI

Week 17 NLP Foundations and Word Embeddings

Day 81Introduction to NLP & Text Preprocessing

The start of language understanding. Overview of NLP applications. Core toolkits: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) and spaCy (industrial-strength NLP). Essential cleaning steps: Tokenization (breaking text into words/sentences), removing special characters, and Stop words removal (common words like 'the', 'a').

Day 82Stemming, Lemmatization & Vectorization

Standardizing and quantifying text. Differences between Stemming (crude removal of suffixes) and Lemmatization (linguistic root form). Techniques for converting text to numerical vectors: Bag of Words (BOW) (count-based) and TF-IDF (Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency, importance-based) implementation using NLTK/sklearn.

Day 83Word Embeddings

Capturing semantic context numerically. Moving beyond sparse vectors. Understanding the core concept of Word2Vec (predicting context or word): Skip-Gram (predicting context from word) & CBOW (Continuous Bag of Words - predicting word from context). Introduction to other dense vector models: GloVe and FastText.

Day 84Sequential Data & RNNs

Handling ordered data like sentences. Defining the need: Why use Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs)? Understanding How RNNs work (hidden state maintaining memory), the process of training RNNs, and the critical challenge of handling the vanishing gradient in long sequences.

Day 85Advanced RNNs & Sequence Tagging

Improving memory and applying to specific tasks. Implementing Bi-Directional RNNs (processing sequence forward and backward). Practical Case Study: Named Entity Recognition (NER) (identifying entities like people/places) and POS Tagging (Part-of-Speech tagging).

Week 18 Advanced Sequence Models and Transformers

Day 86LSTM & GRU

The solution to the vanishing gradient problem. Detailed study of the architecture of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks and the simplified Gated Recurrent Units (GRU). Understanding the function of the internal gates (input, forget, output) and memory cells for long-term dependence.

Day 87Autoencoders

Learning efficient data representations. Understanding the Encoder-Decoder Architecture (compression and reconstruction). Exploring different Types of autoencoders (denoising, variational). Case study on image compression/reconstruction using the MNIST dataset.

Day 88Attention Mechanisms

The revolution in sequence-to-sequence models. A deep dive into How Attention models revolutionized NLP. The Working principles of Attention (selectively focusing on important parts of the input sequence).

Day 89Transformers

The backbone of modern LLMs. The complete Transformer architecture: Self-Attention (contextualizing each token), Multi-Head Attention (multiple attention mechanisms in parallel), and the encoder/decoder stacks. Practical Coding Transformers for various text generation or translation tasks.

Day 90BERT & Advanced NLP

Contextual word embeddings. Introduction to BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers), explaining how it works (masked language modeling, next sentence prediction), and the process of fine-tuning BERT for specific tasks. Case Study: Text Classification and Sentiment Analysis using a pre-trained BERT model.

Week 19 Generative AI and Commercial APIs

Day 91Introduction to Generative AI

The new paradigm of content creation. Defining Generative vs Predictive AI. Comprehensive Overview of Large Language Models (LLMs) (architecture, scale) and their vast industry applications (chatbots, coding, creative content).

Day 92Prompt Engineering

The key skill for interacting with LLMs. Mastering strategic prompting techniques: Zero-shot, One-shot, and Few-shot prompting. Principles of Instruction-based prompt design, advanced Chain-of-Thought techniques, and output control using parameters like temperature and tokens.

Day 93Working with OpenAI

Accessing industry-leading models. Steps for Setting up and authenticating the OpenAI API. Practical Text generation using powerful models like GPT-3.5/GPT-4/GPT-4o.

Day 94Multimodal GenAI

Generating content across modalities. Understanding the architecture and capabilities of models like DALL-E and the process of image generation. Hands-on project: Generating images from textual descriptions using an API.

Day 95Gemini AI

Google's state-of-the-art model. Steps for Obtaining Gemini API keys, exploring the different Gemini models (Nano, Pro, Ultra), and a step-by-step creation of an AI-powered chatbot using the Gemini API.

Week 20 Open-Source LLMs and Deployment

Day 96Open-Source LLMs (LLaMA)

Exploring community-driven models. Introduction to Meta LLaMA (Large Language Model Meta AI), its foundational model architecture, and exploring various variants (8B, 13B, 30B, 70B). Setting up and running the model in a Local setup and performing text generation.

Day 97LangChain Framework - Part 1

Building complex LLM applications. Understanding the Purpose and core components of LangChain (Models, Prompts, Chains, Agents). Setup, dependencies, and basic configuration for building interconnected LLM workflows.

Day 98LangChain Framework - Part 2

Implementing advanced LLM architectures. Building real-world RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) applications with LangChain, which allows LLMs to access external, non-training data sources for grounding answers.

Day 99No-Code/Low-Code AI Agents & Ethics

Autonomous systems and responsible development. Exploring the concept of Autonomous agent risk assessment. Critical discussions on model bias, hallucination, establishing guardrails for safe usage, and following Responsible AI guidelines.

Day 100Month 5 Capstone & Deployment

The final Generative AI project and MLOps completion. Introduction to Git basics and GitHub workflows for version control. Best practices for model saving (serialization). The ultimate goal: Deploying a Generative AI Writing Assistant/Chatbot using Streamlit to create a live, accessible web application.

Month 06 · Weeks 21–24 · Days 101–120

SQL Complete & Business Intelligence (Power BI)

Week 21 SQL Data Definition and Manipulation

Day 101Introduction to Databases

The foundational concepts of data storage. Defining What is Data, the purpose of DBMS vs RDBMS, and the difference between SQL vs MySQL vs NoSQL. Understanding the Client-Server Architecture of databases and introduction to a client tool like Workbench.

Day 102SQL Data Definition & Constraints

Structuring the database. Defining standard Data types (INT, VARCHAR, DATE). Enforcing data integrity using Constraints (PRIMARY KEY, NOT NULL, UNIQUE, DEFAULT, CHECK, FOREIGN KEY). Mastering DDL Commands (Data Definition Language): CREATE, ALTER, DROP, TRUNCATE.

Day 103Data Manipulation & Querying

Adding, modifying, and retrieving data. Mastering DML Commands (Data Manipulation Language): INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE. The core of SQL: DQL (Data Query Language): SELECT, limiting results with LIMIT, and finding unique values with DISTINCT.

Day 104Data Filtering & Operators

Selecting specific records from a table. Filtering data using the essential WHERE clause. Advanced filtering with Operators: pattern matching with LIKE and REGEXP (regular expressions), range checking with BETWEEN, and matching a list of values with IN.

Day 105Grouping & Sorting Data

Summarizing and ordering query results. Aggregating rows using GROUP BY. Filtering aggregated results with HAVING. Ordering the final output with ORDER BY. Using conditional logic within queries via CASE statements. Crucial understanding of the order of query execution (SELECT, FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY).

Week 22 Advanced SQL, Joins, and Windows

Day 106Relational Databases & Keys

Modeling relationships between tables. Understanding the types of Keys: Primary keys, Composite keys, and Foreign keys. Defining Types of relationships (1:1, 1:M, M:M). Introduction to ER diagrams (Entity-Relationship diagrams).

Day 107SQL Joins

Combining data from multiple tables. Implementing and understanding the differences between Inner join (intersection), Left join (all from left), Right join (all from right), Outer join (all rows), Self join, and Cross join.

Day 108Set Operations & Subqueries

Combining query results and nesting queries. Using Set Operations to combine results with same columns: UNION, UNION ALL, EXCEPT, and INTERSECT. Writing and applying various Subqueries: Scalar (returns a single value), Multiple (returns a list of values), and Correlated Subqueries (dependent on outer query).

Day 109Advanced Querying

Techniques for structured, complex queries. Using Derived tables (subqueries in the FROM clause). Mastering Common Table Expressions (CTEs) (named temporary result sets) for query organization. Introduction to Recursive CTEs for hierarchical data.

Day 110Advanced SQL Objects

Beyond basic data retrieval. Deep dive into Window Functions for analytical tasks: LEAD, LAG (accessing rows above/below), FIRST_VALUE, NTILE. Understanding database objects: Views (stored queries), Stored Procedures (stored SQL code), Triggers (actions that fire automatically). Introduction to TCL (Transaction Control Language): COMMIT, ROLLBACK.

Week 23 Excel and Power BI Foundations

Day 111Excel for Analytics Core

Reviewing essential Excel skills for data professionals. Review of advanced Excel capabilities: Statistical/Logical functions (e.g., IF, AND, OR), powerful conditional aggregations like SUMIFS, COUNTIFS, modern Dynamic arrays, lookup functions VLOOKUP, HLOOKUP, and practical Date functions.

Day 112Introduction to Power BI

The start of Business Intelligence. Defining What is BI? Comprehensive Power BI Desktop overview (components). Understanding the Power BI workflow (Get Data -> Transform -> Model -> Visualize). Reviewing Data Import options and navigating the UI.

Day 113Power Query

The Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) layer. Introduction to Power Query for data transformation. Briefing on M Language (the Power Query language). Hands-on with essential transformations: changing datatypes, filtering, and various inbuilt row/column transformations (e.g., unpivot, pivot).

Day 114Advanced Power Query

Complex data shaping techniques. Methods for combining datasets: Appending (stacking) and Merging Queries (joining). Creating utility columns using Indexing and conditional columns based on logic.

Day 115Data Modeling (Power Pivot)

Structuring data for analysis. Introduction to Data Modeling (Star/Snowflake Schema). Defining Relationship Cardinality (1:1, 1:M, M:M) and understanding cross-filter direction. Practical use of the Relationship views to build a robust data model.

Week 24 DAX, Visualization, and Final Capstone

Day 116Introduction to DAX

Data Analysis Expressions for custom calculations. Key difference: Calculated Columns vs Measures (row vs filter context). Understanding DAX syntax, including Logical functions, Text functions, Math, and basic Statistical functions.

Day 117Advanced DAX

Mastering context transition and time intelligence. Advanced Aggregation functions like SUMX and AVERAGEX (iterators). The most important function: the powerful CALCULATE (filter context modification). Understanding Filter functions like ALL and ALLEXCEPT. Implementing Time Intelligence using a Date Dimension table.

Day 118Interactive Visualizations

Building compelling and dynamic reports. Creating standard visuals: Categorical (Bar/Column) and Trend visuals (Line/Area). Utilizing Slicers, performance indicators like KPI cards, and detailed Matrices. Advanced techniques: Drill Through, Drilldown, and integrating Python Script Visuals.

Day 119Power BI Service & Security

Publishing and sharing the final report. The process of Publishing reports from Desktop to Service. Dashboard creation/formatting (pinning visuals). Workspace sharing for collaboration. Implementing Row Level Security (RLS) by defining roles and testing to ensure data access restrictions.

Day 120Final Program Capstone

The grand finale: an end-to-end data science and business intelligence project. End-to-End Business Analytics System: Extracting data using SQL, cleaning in Python/Pandas, creating a predictive model (ML), and finally serving the insights via a deployed Power BI Dashboard with a GenAI-generated executive summary (connecting all six months of learning).

FAQ

About Data Science.

Have a question that isn’t covered here? Ask an advisor directly.

Ask on WhatsApp
Do I need to know programming already?

No. Month 1 starts with what programming is, computational thinking and environment setup (Anaconda, VS Code, Google Colab, Jupyter), then builds up to OOP, NumPy and Pandas.

How much mathematics is involved?

Month 2 is dedicated to statistics and probability — descriptive statistics, distributions, sampling, confidence intervals and hypothesis testing — taught with practical data-science applications.

What deep-learning topics are covered?

Neural networks from perceptrons to backpropagation, activation functions, optimisers, regularisation, Keras and TensorFlow, OpenCV, CNN architectures from LeNet to EfficientNet, transfer learning, R-CNN and YOLO.

What will I do with Generative AI?

Prompt engineering, the OpenAI API, DALL·E image generation, Gemini chatbots, local LLaMA models, LangChain and RAG — ending with a GenAI writing assistant deployed on Streamlit.

Why are SQL and Power BI in a data-science program?

Real projects start in databases and end in dashboards. Month 6 covers SQL end to end and Power BI, culminating in a capstone that connects all six months.
